query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and is intended to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state, but its dynamic behavior across different temperatures and strain rates lacks a theoretical explanation. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could account for this behavior, and what controlled comparison within that regime would distinguish it? Specify predictions relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and a falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In the Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy (HEA), the temperature- and strain-rate-sensitive balance between (i) Shockley partial–mediated planar slip and (ii) deformation twinning is the primary regulator of its flow-stress/ductility behavior. Removal of Co lowers the room-temperature stacking-fault energy (SFE) by ≃5–10 mJ m⁻² relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, so at low–to-ambient temperatures and/or high strain rates the alloy crosses the critical SFE window for mechanical twinning; the dynamic formation of nanoscale twins supplies extra strain hardening that offsets flow localization and preserves ductility. At higher temperatures or slower rates, thermal activation raises the effective SFE and enables cross-slip of perfect dislocations, suppressing twinning; strength drops and strain hardening approaches that of a normal fcc solid solution.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeNiCrMn single-phase fcc solid solution produced by arc melting and homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h, water-quenched; grain size 20–30 µm; no retained precipitates.
generation.intervention: Uniaxial tensile testing over 10⁻³ – 10³ s⁻¹ and 77 K – 873 K, with in-situ high-speed EBSD or synchrotron diffraction to quantify twin volume fraction.
generation.conditions: Same initial microstructure; tests conducted in argon to avoid oxidation; true strain to failure ≥0.6 targeted.
generation.structural_mediator: Density and spatial distribution of deformation twins (nanotwin lamellae 10–50 nm) formed during straining.
generation.mechanism: Lowered SFE in the Co-free alloy reduces the energy barrier for Shockley partial nucleation. At low T or high ε̇, partial dislocation motion outpaces thermally activated cross-slip, so twins nucleate and grow. Twin boundaries block dislocations and raise work-hardening, delaying necking (high ductility) while maintaining high flow stress. At high T or low ε̇, cross-slip restores wavy dislocation glide, suppressing twinning and reducing strain hardening, giving conventional fcc behavior.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with CoCrFeMnNi tested under identical conditions: 1) At 293 K, 10³ s⁻¹ the Co-free alloy will show ~15 % higher 0.2 % proof stress and ~30 % higher uniform elongation. Twin volume fraction ≥4 % vs ≤1 % in the Co-containing alloy. 2) At 673 K, 10⁻³ s⁻¹ both alloys will converge to similar flow stress (<350 MPa) and negligible twinning (<0.5 %). 3) Transition (twinning onset) strain rate will shift to ~2–3 decades slower in the Co-free alloy relative to the Co-containing baseline.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA tested with identical grain size/history.
generation.boundary: Valid for grain sizes 5–50 µm and compositions within ±2 at.% of nominal FeNiCrMn; outside this SFE may differ enough to change mechanisms. Void of second-phase precipitates; applied true strains ≤0.6.
generation.uncertainty: Exact SFE reduction without Co is estimated; quantitative stress/elongation increments may vary ±50 % depending on grain size and interstitial levels.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform interrupted tensile tests at 293 K and 673 K at two strain rates: 10⁻³ s⁻¹ and 10³ s⁻¹, on both alloys. Stop at true strain 0.2 and fracture. Characterize deformed microstructure by TEM/EBSD to measure twin thickness, spacing, and fraction.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If, at 293 K and 10³ s⁻¹, the Co-free alloy shows (a) twin volume fraction <1 % AND (b) work-hardening rate comparable (±10 %) to the Co-containing alloy, OR if at 673 K twins persist (>2 %) in either alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
